Injection of botulinum A toxin into the prostate gland, for the treatment of chronic urinary retention, has shown some promise in small studies. A number of plant extracts such as saw palmetto (Serenoa repens)9 and Pygeum africanum10 are also in use, and the phytosterol sitosterol, which is a constituent of these, is reported to be effective.11 Surgery is recommended for men with more severe symp- toms that do not respond to drug therapy, or who have complications such as acute urinary retention, gross hae- maturia, renal failure, bladder calculi, or recurrent urinary- tract infection. The mainstay of treatment is transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP),1-3 which is more effec- tive than drug treatment but is associated with a risk of complications such as impotence (although this may not be attributable to the surgery in all cases) and bladder neck contracture.2,3 Transurethral incision of the prostate may be used as an alternative for smaller prostates1-3 and open prostatectomy may be indicated for removal of very large glands.3 Various surgical alternatives to TURP use heat to destroy prostatic tissue surrounding the urethra.1-3,12 These minimally invasive therapies include transurethral micro- wave thermotherapy, water-induced thermotherapy, radio- frequency transurethral needle ablation, interstitial laser treatment, and transrectal high-intensity focused ultra- sound. 1.
